paper.title: SEDM: Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory for Agents
paper.central_claim: SEDM selects what agents share (admission by paired replay A/B tests, utility-aware scheduling, cross-domain abstraction) and when recipients use it (Calibrated Memory Gating trained on paired outcomes including ties); it exceeds the strongest evaluated baseline on LoCoMo open-domain questions by 15.1 F1, beats G-Memory on FEVER/HotpotQA with 16-32% fewer prompt tokens, and CMG matches always-use success with about 18% fewer tokens while recovering value from memories that hurt when injected indiscriminately.

signatures.object: Shared agent-society memory store (items with utility weights, tier, provenance) written by candidate extraction from Self-Contained Execution Contexts (SCEC), scheduled by a controller, and read by retrieval with weight-scaled similarity.
signatures.information: SCEC = task input, agent output, summaries of tool calls, seeds and config hashes; ground-truth task reward R(o) (EM / SBERT>=0.7 / accuracy); latency and token deltas. Held-out configuration admits on the e=3 most similar held-out tasks and filters unsolved-source and answer-leaking candidates.
signatures.operation: Paired A/B replay with and without candidate m (k=3 runs per arm) -> S(m)=dR - lambda_L dL - lambda_T dT, accept if S(m)>=eta (eta=0, lambdas=0 in the held-out pipeline); weight init/update from dR; controller cycle: weight update, tier promotion/demotion, merge near-duplicates, distill repeated patterns, isolate conflicting items, decay and remove below minimum; rule-based entity-placeholder abstraction for cross-domain use.
signatures.output: Admitted, weighted, tiered memory set retrieved per query.
signatures.conditions: Original configuration tests on the source task (overestimates utility); held-out configuration adds similar-task tests and answer-leak filters.
signatures.selection_rule: Accept iff mean reward change minus cost penalties >= eta; rejected records kept for audit and never retrieved.
signatures.persistence: Items with weight, usage count, tier, provenance (hashes, seeds, versions); conflict-isolated records retained.
signatures.later_use: Retrieval score sim(q,m)*g(w) then tier/weight ranking for new tasks.
signatures.claimed_effect: LoCoMo open-domain F1 47.5 vs G-Memory 32.4; FEVER 66 vs 62 and HotpotQA EM 39 vs 38 with 16-32% fewer prompt tokens (original configuration).
signatures.failure_boundary: Source-task admission overestimates; under held-out admission the frozen memory gives no gain (0.539 vs 0.544) and the controller-managed memory hurts (0.518 vs 0.534); no rollback or hard size bound described.

retention_trace.selection_data_rule: paired replays (source task in original config; e=3 similar held-out tasks in held-out config), eta=0
retention_trace.measured_gain: original config: FEVER 57->66, HotpotQA 34->39 (single runs); held-out config: -0.5 and -1.6 points when always injected

signatures.object: Recipient-side Calibrated Memory Gating (CMG): Qwen3-4B + LoRA with a linear two-logit head predicting success under skip and under use, temperature-calibrated per action.
signatures.information: Task text plus retrieved memory text only; answers, scores and execution traces are excluded. Training labels come from paired executions with and without M(q) on training tasks.
signatures.operation: Per-action BCE on all four outcome groups (00, 01, 10, 11) including ties; temperature scaling on a calibration split; use memory iff p_use - p_skip > lambda * (estimated injected tokens), lambda chosen on validation.
signatures.conditions: Requires paired runs (doubles execution at training time); memory frozen at gate-training and test time.
signatures.feedback: Observed task success under both actions.
signatures.claimed_effect: Controlled HotpotQA: 0.329 vs always-use 0.333 with 18% fewer agent input tokens; LoCoMo full pipeline 0.556 vs 0.539 and 0.544 with 19-31% fewer tokens than always-use.
signatures.failure_boundary: Frozen memory only; one agent model and one backbone; differences within noise on LoCoMo test; gold-evidence memory is optimistic.

retention_trace.selection_data_rule: held-out validation selects lambda; calibration split fits temperatures
retention_trace.measured_gain: success parity with fewer tokens (HotpotQA); +1.2 to +1.7 points over fixed policies (LoCoMo, within noise)

gap.author_gap: Shared memories can be redundant, misleading or costly for the receiving agent; relevance and past utility do not measure expected improvement over no memory, and winner-only supervision discards the tie cases that carry most of the information.
gap.checked_gap: Largely confirmed and well specified: the paired controlled study shows memory helps on average (+0.084) yet breaks 32 successes while fixing 73, and in the held-out LoCoMo pipeline always-injecting does not help (0.539 vs 0.544) or hurts (0.518 vs 0.534, within noise). The agent-society framing is nominal in the evaluation.

lineage.ancestors: MemoryBank / MemGPT / A-Mem / Mem0 / Zep / LangMem (what to store and retrieve) -> G-Memory (hierarchical multi-agent memory, retrieval base of SEDM) ; adaptive retrieval gates (Self-RAG, FLARE, popularity, complexity classifier) decide whether to retrieve for single generations
lineage.closest_adjacent: G-Memory (ancestor, compared), zero-shot CoT gate and similarity threshold (compared), Self-RAG-style learned gates (described only)
lineage.source_version: as described in 2509.09498v4; neighbour papers are not in the pinned materials

gap.residue: Whether and when to use a retrieved memory for the current task given calibrated marginal gain and token cost; learning online while memory changes is left open.
gap.stakes: Indiscriminate injection more than doubles agent input tokens (2.3x in the controlled study) and can reduce success.
gap.method_response: Verifiable write admission by paired replay, utility-aware scheduling, cross-domain abstraction, and an outcome-supervised cost-aware use gate.
gap.remaining_gap: Held-out evidence that admission/controller improve over an ungoverned store; online co-adaptation of gate and memory; non-QA tasks; other agent models.
unresolved: Full texts of G-Memory, Self-RAG-style gates and Mem0/A-Mem are not pinned; neighbour comparison relies on this paper own description and its Table 1.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus revised. The executed agent-side operation is the main-card definition: a frozen gpt-4o-mini solves new tasks conditioned on retrieved memories with no parameter update; SEDM's contribution decides which entries the conditioning bank holds (paired admission, utility ranking, decay) and whether to inject them (CMG). This matches the run convention for memory systems (r03–r06, sub null when C03's schema/upstream/category-holdout steps are absent). assumption_audit_and_pivot (sol) is rejected: no assumption is relaxed and a guarantee re-derived, and 'relevance ≠ utility' is a motivating empirical observation, not a violated precondition with a tightness or exploit template. outside_taxonomy (son55) is rejected because a card does describe the executed operation; the retention governance lives in the domain layer (H29/H30/H05).

tactic_steps_checked: retrieved memories appended to the agent prompt (only difference between arms)
no per-task parameter update of the agent
C03 schema/upstream-reading/category-holdout steps not executed → sub null
success_checks: conditioning toggled against no-memory on identical executions: met (Tables 4–5)
failure_checks: gate itself is a LoRA-trained Qwen3-4B, outside this card
retention governance not covered by any RS card
matches.reason: Operation-level match; governance and gate are domain-layer content.

Candidates are quarantined until a paired replay passes, rejected items are never retrieved, weights decay and low-weight items are removed with provenance; but eta=0, no hard size bound, no regression budget on solved cases, and held-out evidence that the governed store beats an ungoverned one is absent.
Per-item weights from with/without-memory reward deltas re-rank retrieval; value-stripped ablation shown only in the original configuration (+2 points).

CMG makes memory use a decision with always-use/never-use comparisons on the same store; the trigger is an outcome-trained pre-injection gate (not an uncertainty trigger at reasoning steps) and its generality across backbones is untested.

revision_proposals.text: Add a variant where the access decision is a supervised, calibrated, cost-aware pre-injection gate trained on paired with/without-memory outcomes including ties (distinct from uncertainty-triggered retrieval).
Admission tested on the candidate own source task (self-confirming replay) as a distinct failure from reusing development cases for promotion.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Opus sides with son55. The positive retained-memory numbers (Tables 1–3) come from source-task admission with a controller that updates weights from outcomes on the evaluation stream (opus:O01–O03), so the selection set is not separated from the test set (EVIDENCE rule 2 → at most task). The one clean test of SEDM-produced memory (§4.6, held-out admission, frozen) shows no gain from always using it (opus:O04) and a within-noise gain with CMG; the clean HotpotQA retained store is gold-evidence memory not produced by the SEDM loop.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A calibrated two-head gate trained on paired with/without-memory outcomes (including ties) recovers most of a frozen evidence memory benefit on HotpotQA (0.329 vs 0.333) with about 18% fewer agent input tokens, and in a held-out LoCoMo pipeline is within noise of or slightly above fixed policies with 19-31% fewer tokens; SEDM sender-side admission/scheduling gains are reported only under a source-task admission configuration, on borrowed or single-run baselines.
assessment.not_supported: That SEDM-managed memory improves later tasks under held-out admission; superiority over memory baselines across LoCoMo categories; society-scale sharing benefits.
unresolved: Sample sizes and variance for FEVER/HotpotQA tables
Admission replay and controller cost relative to the reported token savings (opus:O05).

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. CMG (two independent heads on all four paired outcomes, per-action temperature, cost threshold) is fully reconstructable with a tested distinguishing prediction, which would merit 4 alone; but the sender half of the central claim rests on an original admission test that replays the candidate's own source task (self-confirming, conceded by the authors), ad hoc tier/decay constants and an unjustified rule-based abstraction, so the method as claimed is 3.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. CMG attribution is strong (always/skip, similarity, winner head, SFT, CoT, random-gating line, oracle, uncalibrated, three seeds); sender side is weak (cumulative ablation only in the original configuration with test-time weight correction (opus:O02, opus:O01), diffusion not ablated, no ungoverned-store control held-out). Not lowered: the gate half is near-4 and the sender weakness is mostly a holdout defect scored there (A2).

E.holdout.reason: Opus sides with son55. CMG studies use disjoint hashed splits and conversation-level splits (strong), but the headline retained-memory gains use source-task admission plus evaluation-stream weight correction (opus:O01–O03) and were not re-run held-out; the held-out SEDM memory gives no gain (opus:O04); controlled memories are gold evidence; one agent model.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked (A2 ladder). Bootstrap CIs and three gate seeds on HotpotQA but between-gate differences mostly within CIs; LoCoMo 193 questions of one conversation without CI; Tables 1–3 single runs without n or variance.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with sol. Agent tokens, injection rates, gate latency, λ curves and the paired-collection bill ($4.5) are reported, but the headline efficiency claim (16–32% fewer prompt tokens than G-Memory) charges only evaluated-run tokens (opus:O06) while sender-side admission replays k runs × 2 arms × e tasks per candidate (opus:O05) plus controller and LoRA gate training are uncharged — a key coverage gap for a cost claim, so 2 not 3.
